domestic_hazardous.name: Domestic Hazardous & E-Waste
domestic_hazardous.destination: Designated hazardous collection center / Authorised e-waste dismantler

prep_steps: Flatten boxes to save bin space
Remove all shipping tape, staples, and plastic labels
Keep strictly dry
cardboard.tips: Flattened corrugated cardboard can be recycled up to 5-7 times.

light.advice: Tear off or cut out the stained portion. Recycle clean dry parts in the Blue bin.

heavy.advice: Heavily grease/food soaked cardboard (e.g., pizza base) cannot be recycled. Shred and compost in Green bin or discard in Reject.

prep_steps: Remove any plastic film, spiral bindings, or metal clips
Keep clean and dry
Do not shred unless containing private information
paper.tips: Clean newspapers, books, cartons, and paper bags belong in the Blue bin.

light.advice: Tear away soiled sections; dispose of clean paper in the Blue bin.

heavy.advice: Wet, oily, or wax-coated paper cannot be recycled. Dispose in Reject waste.

prep_steps: Empty all liquid and scrape food remnants
Rinse lightly and let air dry
Compress bottles and recap before binning
plastic.tips: Rigid plastics like PET bottles (#1) and HDPE containers (#2) are widely recycled.

light.advice: Give a quick rinse with waste water to avoid attracting pests, then place in Blue bin.

heavy.advice: Wash and dry thoroughly. Unwashed greasy plastic fouls recycling sorting equipment.

prep_steps: Rinse residue thoroughly
Remove metal lids or plastic rings
Handle carefully to prevent breakage
glass.tips: Glass is 100% recyclable indefinitely without loss of purity or quality.

attributes_by_color.clear: Clear (Flint) glass has the highest recycling demand. Place in Blue bin.
attributes_by_color.green: Green glass is sorted separately at MRF facilities for colored bottle re-melting.
attributes_by_color.brown: Brown (Amber) glass protects UV-sensitive beverages and is recycled back into amber bottles.
attributes_by_color.other: Mirrors, window panes, and borosilicate glassware contain additives; do not mix with regular container glass.

light.advice: Rinse bottle before placing in Blue bin.

heavy.advice: Clean off dried sludge or food thoroughly before recycling.

prep_steps: Empty completely and rinse cans
Tuck sharp tin lids inside cans
Crush aluminum beverage cans to save space
metal.tips: Aluminum and steel cans save up to 95% energy when recycled compared to raw bauxite ore smelting.

light.advice: Rinse off food particles and place in Blue bin.

heavy.advice: Wash with water. If containing hazardous chemicals/paints, take to Red bin instead.

prep_steps: Do not wrap in plastic or polybags
Drain excess liquids before binning
Drop into home compost bin or green municipal collection
organic.tips: Organic waste produces nutrient-rich compost or biogas when segregated at source.

prep_steps: NEVER dispose in regular Blue or Green household bins
Tape lithium-ion battery terminals with clear tape to prevent short circuits and fires
Store in a dry cool box away from sunlight
battery_ewaste.tips: Batteries and electronics contain heavy metals (lead, cadmium, lithium) and must go to certified e-waste recyclers.

light.advice: Deliver to municipal hazardous collection booth or electronic retailer drop-off bin.

heavy.advice: If leaking or corroded, handle with gloves, place in a sealed bag, and take to hazardous collection.

prep_steps: If wearable, donate to charity or local NGOs
Worn-out textiles can be repurposed as cleaning rags
Keep clean and dry before binning
textile.tips: Clean fabric scraps and rags go into the Blue dry waste stream for fiber upcycling.

light.advice: Wash and dry, then reuse or deposit in dry waste bin.

heavy.advice: Soiled with oil, paint or chemical residues? Dispose in Reject black bin.

prep_steps: Ensure no recyclable items are mixed in
Wrap sanitary waste securely before placing in reject bin
Keep separate from wet organic waste
general_trash.tips: This waste goes to landfill or waste-to-energy plants. Aim to minimize non-recyclable purchases.
